approach.method_basis: The Parent is a molecular-graph genetic algorithm steered by a Gaussian-process batch selector. It learns only from the current objective's accepted scores. It keeps the 64 best scored molecules as breeders and samples parents from high-scoring quantile bands. Each breeding attempt does one of two things. In about 45% of attempts (halved after long runs of failed attempts) it recombines two parents, joining a large connected fragment of one to a small fragment of the other through a single bond, sometimes followed by one extra edit. Otherwise it walks one parent through one to three random atom, bond or ring edits, and the walk lengthens when generation saturates. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen swaps are disabled. Canonical identities reject duplicates. An admission gate refuses offspring that introduce sulfur environments beyond those already present in their scored parents. Each batch of ten is chosen from a fresh pool of 160 candidates by correlated Thompson draws from a Gaussian process. The process uses count-based Morgan fingerprints with a Tanimoto-style kernel and is refitted on every accepted observation.
approach.novelty: This experiment switches crossover off only while the search is stalled, to ask whether recombination still helps then. A counter tracks consecutive batches of ten that fail to raise the session's best score. Once three in a row fail, every breeding attempt in the following batches that would have recombined takes the ordinary single-parent mutation walk instead. Crossover returns as soon as a batch improves the best score. Until the first stall the run is identical to the Parent, so any difference comes from what happens during and after stalls. An earlier sibling removed crossover for the whole run and lost, but that result cannot separate stalled phases from improving phases. The three siblings in this round change how stalled batches search, through more Thompson noise, longer mutation walks or a larger candidate pool. This one instead removes recombination during the same stalls.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent spends a measurable part of its budget in stagnation, and the evidence does not show whether its heavily used crossover route still contributes there. Its three summary.json/run.log pairs are complete at 1500 calls per seed: macro mean 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878, seed macros 0.643098, 0.563173 and 0.583088. Recomputed at planning from all fifteen Parent trajectories, the shared stall counter reaches 3 in 13 of 15 sessions: 29 episodes (4 terminal-censored) and 91 of 435 announced batches (3.14 batches per episode). The counter never reaches 3 in deco_hop seeds 0 and 2. Mean per-session best-so-far gain decays from +0.2402 over evaluations 11-100 to +0.1054 over 101-200 and +0.0424 over 201-300. The leading sets are founder-concentrated: n-9f11b684e560 records four sessions per panel whose ten leaders trace to one founder. A streaming audit of the fifteen Parent task logs found that, inside those 91 stalled batches, the Parent still requests crossover in 7,094 of 15,928 multi-survivor attempts (44.5%), pools 6,144 crossover products and emits 281 crossover offspring among 910 (30.9%). There, crossover no longer outperforms mutation per emission. Sequential incumbent-gain mass per emission is 0.000557 for crossover and 0.000509 for mutation in stalled batches, against 0.001815 and 0.001411 (1.29x) outside them. Crossover supplies 7 of the 25 stall-ending best offspring, close to its emission share. Strict parent-beat rates fall from 15.1% to 6.4% for crossover and from 17.4% to 9.5% for mutation. These are posterior-selected, accepted-only streams without counterfactual labels, and the crossover hurdle is the better of two parents. The whole-run removal n-6059424cc614 lost 0.043640 (seed deltas -0.103844, -0.001329, -0.025747) and answered unconditional presence. It diverged from the first batch and changed every phase, so it cannot say whether that contribution is carried by improving phases alone. Its loss also lies inside this Anchor's departure band: all 28 complete children lose on average, from -0.183 for n-04741f9b1832 to -0.016 for n-da0eeecfb462, with median -0.049. Older ungated controls n-767d2ce08797 and n-1faebb978a01, on Parents n-62daf219c70a and an exchange-containing Parent, and the BRICS construction variant n-55d120396e72 keep their own conditions.

literature_review.conclusion: Theory predicts that crossover's value is concentrated at local optima, but only while the population retains diversity. Campaign receipts show crossover losing its per-emission advantage over mutation in this Anchor's founder-concentrated stalls. The registered non-inferiority prediction is therefore a genuine test against the stall-escape alternative. The second query found no matched molecular stagnation result, and the Chemical Science 2020 diversity-enforcing follow-up page returned HTTP 403, so it adds no evidence.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The intervention, trigger, K=3 and classification are fixed by the frozen ticket and grounded in the Anchor's own receipts: trajectory-derived stall exposure, per-route stalled versus unstalled yield from the fifteen task logs, the whole-run removal, and the departure band of all 28 complete children. No borrowed external element enters the code. The theory source only frames the two competing predictions the experiment discriminates.

sources.applicability: Supplies a competing prediction, not an implemented element. If recombination is the stall-escape route, removing it during stagnation should lengthen stalls and lose. If founder concentration has removed the diversity crossover needs, it should be dispensable there. Bit-string Jump_k, the (mu+1) population and asymptotic bounds do not transfer quantitatively to molecular graphs, a Thompson-selected batch of ten or a 300-evaluation Top-1 panel.
sources.finding: Runtime analysis of the (mu+1) GA on Jump_k. Once the population sits on the local optimum, mutation creates new plateau points, and crossover of different species followed by mutation can trigger a sudden burst of diversity. This reaches the optimum a factor of about n faster than mutation alone, and both operators are described as vital. The introduction also states that without sufficient diversity in the population, crossover is not effective.
sources.title: Dang, Friedrich, Koetzing, Krejca, Lehre, Oliveto, Sudholt and Sutton, Escaping Local Optima using Crossover with Emergent or Reinforced Diversity (arXiv:1608.03123)

hypothesis: While the session's own count of consecutive non-improving announced batches is at least K=3, set the effective connected-fragment crossover probability to zero for every breeding attempt of the next announced batch. The original crossover-branch uniform draw stays at its stream position, so each such attempt takes the inherited single-parent mutation walk with its sampled one/two/three-call length, saturation floor and unchanged operators. Crossover, partner selection, fragment construction and post-crossover finishing are untouched before the first trigger and resume unchanged from the batch after the first improving batch.

finding_summary.headline: Crossover switched off only during stalls: stalls did not lengthen, yet the matched mean fell 0.014 with all three seeds lower
finding_summary.insights:
Recombination is not dispensable during stalls on this Anchor, but the result does not support the stall-escape story that would most simply explain why. That story needed stalls to lengthen and stall yield to fall; stall length was unchanged and yield fell only about 6%. The theory-based alternative, that crossover stops helping once the population has lost diversity, predicted a harmless removal and is contradicted at the endpoint even though founder concentration stayed at the Parent's level. The one stall-phase difference that tracks the loss is how far a stall break reaches and how much recombinant material the population carries forward afterwards, so crossover may matter more for the size of the escape than for its timing. These are single-realization signatures, not identified causes.

The loss must also be read against departure from the Anchor's own run. Once a session first stalls its future is re-randomized, and the four cells where the Parent gained most after its first stall carry about 83% of the summed loss, exactly where the Anchor's continuation was a favourable draw. Crossover's stall contribution is therefore not separated from departure from the Anchor's realized continuation. Against a pure-departure reading, this Child lost more than each of the three same-trigger siblings, both panel-wide (their changes were -0.010, +0.008 and +0.005) and in those same cells; but the siblings are interventions in their own right, not null controls.

Together with the earlier whole-run removal (-0.044), this shows that switching recombination off costs endpoint score whether it is removed throughout or only while the search is stalled, which closes the idea that stalled batches offer free capacity by switching recombination off. The molecular assessment finds chemistry essentially identical to the Parent's, including the tiny fragments that only the recombination route wastes evaluations on (104 versus 105), so chemistry does not explain the score. This route registered one complete answer, and no threshold or probability sweep is justified. What remains open is the size of the departure effect that every stall-conditioned sibling shares: a stall-triggered change to the random stream alone, or more seeds, would measure it.
finding_summary.results:
The switch worked exactly as registered. Thirteen of the fifteen task sessions stalled at least once, giving 90 stalled batches in 30 episodes; the two decoration-hopping sessions that never stall reproduced the Parent molecule for molecule, and every other session matched the Parent exactly up to its first stalled batch. Inside stalled batches about 6,900 breeding attempts that would have recombined took the ordinary mutation walk instead, and not one partner draw, recombinant, finishing edit or crossover offspring appeared. Outside them crossover ran at the Parent's rate (45.6% of attempts versus 45.4%).

Stalls did not get longer. The Child spent 90 batches stalled against the Parent's 91 (30 episodes versus 29, four left unfinished in each). Of the 13 first stalls, which start from identical states, 4 lasted longer, 3 shorter and 6 the same. Yield inside stalls barely moved: incumbent gain per evaluated molecule was 0.000492 versus 0.000524 (28 improving molecules in both), and 8.3% versus 8.6% of offspring beat their best parent. What did shrink was the jump that ends a stall: in 8 of the 13 matched first stalls the breaking batch gained less than the Parent's, and the 13 breaks summed to 0.261 versus 0.390, most visibly in sitagliptin seeds 0 and 1 (about 0.033 versus 0.087 and 0.099). Recombinants also became scarcer in the breeding population: at stall ends 17% of the 64 survivors and 17% of the top ten had themselves been made by crossover, versus 26% and 28% in the Parent, and at session end only 1 of 15 best molecules came from crossover, versus 6 of 15. Founder concentration among the leaders stayed as high as in the Parent.

The matched mean fell from 0.5965 to 0.5823, a change of -0.0142, and all three seed scores fell (-0.024, -0.006, -0.013). Ten of fifteen cells fell (one by a negligible 0.00000005), three rose and two (unexposed) were identical. The loss sits mainly in zaleplon seed 0 (-0.074), sitagliptin seed 2 (-0.079), zaleplon seed 1 (-0.034) and sitagliptin seed 0 (-0.027), partly offset by zaleplon seed 2 (+0.022); dropping any single cell leaves a mean between -0.016 and -0.009. Unlike every earlier complete child of this Anchor, it keeps the Parent's late decoration-hopping breakthrough, because that session never stalls. Under the frozen rule this classifies as a positive contribution of crossover during stagnation, and the registered prediction that removal would be harmless is falsified.

molecular.headline: Flat halogen-heavy polyaromatic amides: a few genuinely drug-like leaders beside N-halogen, nitroso and nine-membered aromatic rings
molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives this node proposed 870 molecules per panel (4350 total, 876-879 unique per panel), and the chemistry is uniform: medium-sized, almost entirely flat, ring-dense and heavily halogenated. The digest's string-level counters read ring_closure_rate 0.971-0.984 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.963-0.976 on every panel, and RDKit agrees: median 3-4 rings and 2-4 aromatic rings per molecule, median heavy-atom count 25-31 and median MW 371-451. Halogenation is the dominant decoration (halogen_rate 0.79-0.98 on four panels, 0.15 on one), charged_rate is 0.0000-0.0011 and stereocentre_rate is exactly 0.0000 everywhere. The best molecules are two-to-five-ring heteroaromatic amides, carboxamides or fused azine-ones; the worst, on four of five panels, are 1-5 heavy-atom fragments. Quality is bimodal. One panel's leaders are real medicinal chemistry (benzazepine-like tricyclics, QED 0.61-0.74, SA 3.0-3.6) while another's are strained and over-functionalised (QED 0.15-0.41, SA 4.5-6.0). Every panel's leading set is founder-concentrated: on each of the five objectives every proposal within 0.01 of the panel best comes from one seed only, and on one panel eight distinct proposals share the exact score 0.440491 while differing only in which halogen sits where. Comparison is complete: context.comparison reports child_complete and paired_complete true against code Parent n-1744a1494180, and all 15 Child and 15 Parent trajectory files named in the brief were present and readable; none was missing. Chemistry is near-identical to the Parent on most measures, and on deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 the Child's 300 proposals are the same molecules in the same order as the Parent's. The visible Child-specific chemical shifts are narrow: more halogen on nitrogen on one panel (480 of 870 proposals versus the Parent's 275), an 81-molecule family carrying nine-membered aromatic rings that the Parent barely explores (80 such rings versus 1), and more ten-membered-and-larger rings on another panel (158 proposals versus 37).

per_task.generated_character: Medium, flat, tri- or bicyclic heteroaromatic carboxamides and anilides. Score span 0.0000-0.4594 with median 0.3229; median 25 heavy atoms, MW 307-489, 3 rings and 3 aromatic rings, logP ~4.5, TPSA ~56. Two leader families. The seed-2 family is an indole/benzothiophene-2-carboxamide bearing a free N-amino amide (hydrazide) and an aldimine, with a cyclobuta-fused variant at the top (0.4594, 6-4-6 ring set, QED 0.38, SA 3.4). The seed-1 family at 0.4405 is built on a nine-membered aromatic ring fused to a pyridine with a halogen on the ring nitrogen. The seed-0 family is a methylthio/methylamino indole carboxamide with an N-fluorinated ring nitrogen (0.3850). All descend visibly from the supplied 3,4,5-trimethoxy indole-2-carboxamide founder, which was the highest-scoring initial molecule at 0.3051.
liabilities: halogen bonded to nitrogen in 480 of 870 proposals, 453 of them on an aromatic ring nitrogen, including 8 of the 12 digest leaders
nine-membered aromatic rings in 81 proposals (80 such rings) carrying an N-Br, forming the whole 0.4405 leader family
free hydrazide N-N in 32.2% of the top decile and an N-hydroxy hydrazide in the final batch
non-ring aldimine C=N in 21.8% of the top decile, a group that hydrolyses on contact with water
chloromethyl aryl ether (OCCl) in the final-batch leaders, an alkylating electrophile
cyclobuta-fused benzene in the single best molecule, a strained and oxidation-prone ring system
22 proposals of 1-5 heavy atoms scoring 0.0000, 6 of them spent after evaluation 200 of 300
missing_features: no trifluoromethyl group in any of the 870 proposals, so fluorine never appears as the carbon-bound CF3 of the reference chemistry
no N,N-dialkyl acetamide side chain; the amide nitrogen carries aryl, NH2, NHOH or halogen instead
no aryl nitrile: nitrile occurs in 2 of 870 proposals although the initial population supplied one
no pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine or other fused 5-6 N-bridged bicycle; the fused bicycles are indole, benzothiophene and cyclobuta-fused benzenes
no saturated N-heterocycle at all (piperidine/piperazine motif in 0 of 870), so every basic centre would be an open chain
no stereochemistry specified anywhere (stereocentre_rate 0.0000)
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score rises with aromatic ring count and amide content and falls off to zero for anything that loses a ring: amide occurs in 67.8% of the panel and 67.8% of the top decile versus 49.4% of the bottom decile, aromatic rings median 3 at the top versus 2 at the bottom, and all 22 one-to-five-atom proposals scored exactly 0.0000. Above about 0.42 the gradient goes flat on halogen identity: 8 distinct proposals share the score 0.440491 and differ only in F/Cl/Br permutation at the ring nitrogen and the pendant azine, so eight oracle calls bought no information. Basic amine centres move the wrong way here (5.4% of the panel, 1.1% of the top decile, 14.9% of the bottom).

per_task.generated_character: The largest and least drug-like molecules of the five panels. Score span 0.5000-0.8561, median 0.5963; median 31 heavy atoms, MW ~450, 4 rings, 10 H-bond acceptors, TPSA 127, QED 0.29, SA 4.1, and a maximum SMILES length of 191 characters. The seed-0 leaders (0.80-0.8561) are five-ring fused purine/triazinone-like cores with a pendant chloro-quinazoline, four bridgehead atoms, a ring thione and an O-F bond, and SA climbs to 6.0. The seed-2 leaders (0.64) are an entirely different object: a biphenylene-type system of fused four-membered aromatic rings carrying two nitroso groups, an aryl methyl ketone and an aldehyde. The 1-3 atom fragments all score exactly 0.5000, the panel floor, so the objective gives the optimizer no signal against them.
liabilities: O-F hypofluorite bonds in all eight seed-0 leaders including the panel best at 0.8561; this bond does not survive isolation
alpha-chloro, alpha-fluoro ethers (C(F)OCCl) in the leaders, doubly activated alkylating agents
two nitroso groups on the seed-2 leader family, genotoxic and tautomerically unstable
four-membered aromatic rings in 87 proposals (168 such rings), a biphenylene-like motif that is not an accessible building block
4 bridgehead atoms and 1-3 unassigned stereocentres per seed-0 leader, with SA score reaching 6.0
49.4% of the panel carries at least one unassigned potential stereocentre, rising to 64.4% in the top decile
22 proposals of 1-5 heavy atoms, all scoring at the 0.5000 panel floor
missing_features: no sulfonamide or sulfone anywhere in the 870 proposals, despite the initial population supplying an aryl sulfonamide
no secondary aryl amide linker of the kind that would hold a decorating group at a defined vector; amide occurs in only 2.5% of the panel
no basic amine centre (5.2% overall, 1.1% of the top decile), so the scaffolds carry no ionisable handle
no saturated piperidine/piperazine linker (1 of 870 proposals)
the polar enrichment the score rewards is supplied by nitroso and aldehyde rather than by any stable H-bond acceptor such as sulfone, sulfoxide or tertiary amide
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks size and polar decoration: top decile median 32 heavy atoms and TPSA 134 against bottom decile 25 and 74. The strongest single correlates in the panel are nitroso (27.6% overall, 55.2% of the top decile, 5.7% of the bottom) and aldehyde (12.5% overall, 51.7% of the top decile), with nitrile also enriched (29.2% / 36.8%). Peroxide O-O runs the other way (9.0% overall, 0% of the top decile). Because the floor is 0.5000, losing the whole molecule costs the same as any ordinary poor molecule, and 22 degenerate fragments were evaluated at that floor.

per_task.generated_character: The most convincing chemistry of the five panels. Score span 0.00017-0.9999994, median 0.7072. The seed-1 leaders at 1.0000 are 2,3,4,5-tetrahydro-1H-3-benzazepine-like tricyclics: a seven-membered N-heterocycle fused to a chlorophenyl, a pendant ethyl/fluoro/phenol aryl, and an N-(4-aminobutyl) arm. They are 26-28 heavy atoms, MW 375-468, QED 0.61-0.74, SA 3.0-3.6, logP ~5.3, TPSA ~32: molecules a chemist would recognise and could make. The seed-2 family at 0.91-0.95 is less clean, replacing the fused tricycle with a chromane bearing an exocyclic enamine onto a four-membered azete ring and a benzyl chloride. The lowest scorers are the supplied dichlorophenyl proline sulfonamides and their early descendants at 0.0002-0.0016.
liabilities: benzylic chloride CH2Cl in 17.5% of the panel including the seed-2 final leaders, a reactive alkylating group
four-membered azete/azetine rings bearing an exocyclic enamine in the seed-2 leaders, neither isolable nor configurationally stable
allene and cumulated double bonds in the final-batch leaders (cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.0023)
logP above 5 in the top decile with TPSA near 32, a profile that would fail ordinary developability screens
23 proposals of 1-5 heavy atoms, 11 of them spent after evaluation 200 of 300
O-halogen bonds in 75 proposals and N-halogen bonds in 35
missing_features: the basic nitrogen is almost never in a ring of its own: piperidine/piperazine motif in 5 of 870 proposals, so the pharmacophore is carried by a flexible 4-aminobutyl chain (median 7 rotatable bonds)
no aryl piperazine or arylalkyl piperazine, the ordinary way this basic centre is presented in real ligands of this class

no stereochemistry: 96.3% of the panel carries at least one unassigned potential stereocentre and every 1.0000-scoring leader carries two, so each reported leader is actually a mixture of up to four diastereomers
no amide or sulfonamide in the top decile at all, so the leaders have essentially one H-bond donor and no directed polar contact beyond the phenol
no second aromatic ring beyond two (median 2 aromatic rings), limiting the extended biaryl geometry available
per_task.score_gradient_reading: One feature dominates everything else: a basic aliphatic amine, present in 82.2% of the panel, 100% of the top decile and 19.5% of the bottom decile. The gradient then rewards lipophilic halogenated aryl and punishes polar acidic groups: sulfonamide 50.6% of the bottom decile against 0% of the top, carboxylic acid 35.6% against 0%, amide 47.1% against 0%; top decile logP 5.33 and TPSA 32.5 against bottom decile 3.95 and 95.8. Above 0.96 the gradient flattens on substituent identity, with 4 proposals sharing the exact score 0.963157 across F/Cl/Br and CH2OH/CH2SH swaps.

per_task.generated_character: The narrowest panel. Score span 0.0000-0.2314, median 0.1861, and the top 35 proposals all come from seed 2 on one scaffold: a 2-propylquinoline attached to a ten- to twelve-membered macrolactam containing two amide carbonyls and two N-methyl amine nitrogens, with a vinylogous amide (enamine) at the ring junction. Median 30 heavy atoms, MW ~409, QED 0.67-0.78, SA 3.3-3.5. This is the only panel with little halogen (halogen_rate 0.1517, median 0 halogens). 396 of 870 proposals contain a ring of 8 or more atoms and 158 contain a ring of 10 or more. Bridged 9-membered variants appear among the leaders with 2 bridgehead atoms and SA rising to 4.9.
liabilities: ten- to twelve-membered macrolactams in the entire leading set; medium rings of this size are among the hardest to close synthetically
a vinylogous amide / push-pull enamine at the macrocycle junction in 90.8% of the top decile, which will tautomerise and hydrolyse
halogen on an amine nitrogen (N-Cl) inside a leading macrocycle at 0.2267
N-S single bonds (sulfenamide) and an N-O single bond appearing in the final batch at 0.2105 and 0.2082
bridged 9-membered leaders with 2 bridgehead atoms and 2 unassigned stereocentres, SA 4.8-4.9
13 proposals of 1-5 heavy atoms scoring 0.0000, and 10 distinct proposals sharing the score 0.0000
missing_features: no sulfonamide (1 of 870 proposals), so one of the two reference pharmacophores this median objective interpolates is structurally unrepresented
no fused bicyclic lactam or methylenedioxyphenyl-type system; the second ring system is always the same quinoline inherited from the initial population
the basic nitrogens are only ever N-methyl amines inside a large flexible macrocycle, never a discrete piperazine ring (3.9% of the panel)
no aryl sulfone, aryl ether biaryl or other rigid polar linker; the connection between the quinoline and the macrocycle is a single bond to an sp2 or sp3 carbon
no specified stereochemistry although 63.2% of the panel has at least one unassigned potential stereocentre
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Three co-occurring features separate the deciles cleanly: the quinoline (51.3% of the panel, 97.7% of the top decile, 12.6% of the bottom), a basic aliphatic amine (46.6% / 94.3% / 18.4%) and an amide (77.9% / 96.6% / 39.1%); the vinylogous amide tracks them at 46.6% / 90.8% / 13.8%. Ester runs the other way (14.0% overall, 0% of the top decile, 35.6% of the bottom). The whole top of the panel sits inside 0.005 of itself on one scaffold, so the gradient near the ceiling is about macrocycle ring size and N-substituent identity rather than about scaffold choice at all.

per_task.generated_character: Nitrogen-rich fused bicycles, aggressively fluorinated in the wrong places. Score span 7.7e-27 to 0.6668, median 0.1608; median 26 heavy atoms, MW ~371, 4 rings, 2 aromatic rings, TPSA 77, QED 0.72, SA 4.7. The seed-0 leaders are a pyrrolo-pyrimidinone / triazinone-like fused core carrying an exocyclic imine, a fluorine on the ring nitrogen, an N-fluoromethyl group, a pendant azetidine or thiazolidine, and a fluorinated cyclopentene or anisole. The seed-2 family substitutes a 1-fluoro-cyclopentadienol for the aryl ring. 269 of 870 proposals contain a three- or four-membered ring and 50 contain a three-membered ring perceived as aromatic.
liabilities: N-F bonds in 272 proposals, 263 of them on aromatic ring nitrogen, including the panel best at 0.6668 and 67.8% of the top decile
O-F hypofluorite bonds in 198 proposals including leaders at 0.6144 and 0.5911
fluoromethylamine N-CH2F groups on nearly every leader, which release formaldehyde and fluoride
three-membered rings perceived as aromatic in 50 proposals, and a 3-membered ring in the final batch
cyclopentadienol and non-aromatic cyclopentene-diol motifs that would tautomerise immediately
24 proposals of 1-5 heavy atoms (F, FF, CF, FCl) scoring 0.0000, 8 of them after evaluation 200 of 300
SA score median 4.7, the highest of the five panels, with leaders at 5.2-5.5
missing_features: no trifluoromethyl group in any of the 870 proposals, even though the score gradient clearly rewards fluorine count; the generator places F on nitrogen (272 proposals) and on oxygen (198) instead of accumulating it on one carbon
no 2,4,5-trifluorophenyl or any other multiply-fluorinated single aromatic ring; aryl C-F occurs in 227 proposals but almost never more than once per ring
no beta-amino amide; amide occurs in 2.4% of the panel and the basic nitrogen is instead a ring NH of an azetidine, pyrrolidine or thiazolidine
no triazolopiperazine or other saturated fused N-heterocycle; the fused systems are aromatic azinones
no specified stereochemistry, although 70.9% of the panel carries an unassigned potential stereocentre and this objective's reference chemistry is a single enantiomer
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Halogen count is the clearest driver: median 3 halogens in the top decile against 1 in the bottom, with N-halogen at 67.8% of the top decile against 14.9% of the bottom and a basic amine centre at 52.9% against 11.5%. Score also rises with nitrogen count (median 5 at the top, 3 at the bottom) and with ring count (4 against 3). The panel is brutally sharp: the digest median is 0.1608 against a best of 0.6668, single-atom and diatomic proposals score exactly 0.0000, and one final-batch molecule that differs from a 0.38-scoring sibling by one ring bond scores 0.0129.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across all 4350 proposals of this node (n-9e5f01d67b9f, Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per objective) not one molecule contains a trifluoromethyl group, while 889 carry a halogen bonded to nitrogen and 335 carry one bonded to oxygen. On two panels this is the majority motif: 480 of 870 and 272 of 870 proposals place a halogen on nitrogen, 453 and 263 of them on an aromatic ring nitrogen. The generator's own leaders carry it: the N-bromo nine-membered-ring family at 0.4405, the O-F bearing fused cores at 0.8561 and 0.6144, and the N-fluoro panel best at 0.6668. Where halogen count visibly drives score, the top decile reaches a median of only 3 halogens scattered over heteroatoms rather than concentrated on carbon. Measured with RDKit over the trusted search trajectories; comparable in the code Parent n-1744a1494180 (0 trifluoromethyl, 786 N-halogen, 217 O-halogen), so this is an inherited generator property rather than a new one.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator attaches halogens one at a time to whichever heavy atom an operator selects, including ring nitrogen and oxygen, and never builds a polyhalogenated carbon centre.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make halogen substitution element-aware: permit halogen attachment to carbon freely, and to nitrogen, oxygen or sulfur only when the generating parent already carried that heteroatom-halogen bond. Separately, add a substitution that installs a whole polyhalogenated carbon group as one unit, so that multi-halogen carbon centres are reachable without passing through intermediates that single-atom edits would never assemble. Both are local operator constraints and need no knowledge of what is being optimized.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Of 4350 proposals, 76 contain a sulfonamide and 145 contain any S=O, and on three of the five panels the count across all 870 proposals is exactly zero even though the same ten initial molecules, including an aryl dichlorophenyl sulfonamide, seeded every panel. On the one panel where sulfonamides persist they sit entirely in the low-scoring inherited region (50.6% of the bottom score decile, 0% of the top). The operator set the node logs is replace_atom, append_atom, delete_atom, insert_atom, change_bond, close_ring and open_ring, none of which can reach S(=O)(=O)N without intermediate states that are not valid molecules. Counts identical in the code Parent (76 and 145).
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot construct an oxidized-sulfur functional group; sulfonyl and sulfonamide groups only ever appear by inheritance from the supplied population.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add group-level substitutions that install and remove whole oxidized-heteroatom functional groups (sulfonyl, sulfonamide, sulfoxide, and the same argument applies to nitro and phosphoryl) as single atomic edits. Single-atom operators make entire classes of ordinary polar medicinal chemistry unreachable unless a seed molecule happens to supply them, which silently restricts the reachable space in a way no amount of search can repair.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 104 of 4350 proposals are 1-5 heavy atoms: single atoms, dihalogens, hydrazine, acetylene, hydrogen cyanide and nitric oxide, appearing as the worst entries of four of the five digest panels. They scored 0.0000 on three panels and sat at the objective floor on another, and 30 of them were spent after evaluation 200 of a 300-call budget, one of them as the second-to-last evaluation of a session. All 104 were emitted on the two-parent recombination route according to the node's own offspring_observed provenance, and none occurred in any batch in which that route was inactive. The code Parent emitted 105 of them, so the liability is a property of the recombination route itself and not of this node's change.
transferable_gaps.gap: The recombination route can return a one-to-five-atom fragment instead of a recombinant, and nothing downstream rejects it before it consumes an oracle call.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Admit a recombination product only if it retains a floor of structure relative to its generating parents, for example a minimum heavy-atom count and at least as many rings as the smaller parent, and re-draw instead of emitting when that floor fails. The pool is already generated with a bounded attempt loop, so a rejected fragment costs a retry rather than an evaluation. This is a property of the proposal, checkable without any objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring census over the trusted trajectories: one panel contains 80 nine-membered aromatic rings in 81 molecules, another 168 four-membered aromatic rings in 87 molecules, a third 50 three-membered aromatic rings, and a fourth 143 ten-membered plus 34 eleven-membered rings. These are not rare accidents in the tail, they are in the leading sets: the eight-molecule 0.4405 family is built on a nine-membered aromatic ring, the 0.6442 family on fused four-membered aromatic rings, the 0.4594 panel best on a cyclobuta-fused benzene, and an entire leading set of 35 proposals on ten- to twelve-membered macrolactams. The Parent shows the same capability with a different distribution (1 nine-membered aromatic ring, 165 four-membered aromatic rings, 72 three-membered aromatic rings), so the insensitivity is inherited while the realized sizes drift from run to run.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring construction is insensitive to ring size and ring strain, producing three-, four-, nine- and twelve-membered rings that the generator then presents as ordinary aromatic or saturated systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Give the ring-forming and ring-opening operators a size preference: restrict new conjugated rings to five, six and seven members, restrict new saturated rings to three through seven, and reject a closure whose resulting ring exceeds a declared maximum. Size and conjugation of the formed ring are properties of the proposed graph, so this constraint is entirely task-blind, and it is cheap because ring closure and ring opening are the two lowest-weight operators in the set.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Beyond the N-halogen and O-halogen bonds already counted, the leading sets carry nitroso groups (27.6% of one panel and 55.2% of its top decile), free hydrazides (41.4% of another top decile), alpha-halo ethers (27.6% of a top decile), chloromethyl ethers inside final-batch leaders, sulfenamide N-S and hydroxylamine N-O single bonds appearing in final batches, and non-ring aldimines (21.8% of a top decile). Each arises from a single-atom edit placing a halogen or an N/O/S atom adjacent to an existing heteroatom. This re-observes and widens the gap already recorded for the code Parent n-1744a1494180, whose own molecular assessment states that a narrow sulfur envelope leaves substantial environment-dependent sulfur and non-sulfur reactivity unresolved; the same conditions apply, at 300 observations per objective on Search seeds 0, 1 and 2.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator creates heteroatom-heteroatom and alpha-halo-heteroatom bonds freely, so its highest-scoring molecules carry functional groups that cannot be isolated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Evaluate the newly created local environment rather than the whole molecule: when an edit forms a bond between two heteroatoms, or places a halogen on a carbon already bonded to oxygen or nitrogen, require that the generating parent already contained that same local environment, and otherwise offer the conventional alternative that keeps the scaffold intact. A per-edit environment rule generalises the existing narrow single-element containment to the reactive classes that currently dominate the leaders, and it is defined purely on the proposed graph.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest's string-level stereocentre_rate is exactly 0.0000 on all five panels, yet RDKit finds at least one unassigned potential stereocentre in 96.3%, 70.9%, 63.2%, 49.4% and 9.0% of the respective panels' proposals. The leaders are the worst affected: every molecule in one panel's top decile carries an unassigned centre, the 1.0000-scoring leaders carry two each, and one leading fused system carries three. This reproduces a gap already recorded for the code Parent and, per its assessment, originating further up the code ancestry; it persists unchanged here under the same conditions, Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per objective.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits flat SMILES with no stereochemical specification, so most of what it proposes is an unresolved mixture rather than a molecule.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Either carry explicit configuration through the edit, assigning it when an operator creates a new sp3 centre and preserving it when an edit leaves one untouched, or bias substitution toward achiral patterns so that fewer unresolved centres are created. Whether a centre is potentially stereogenic is a property of the graph, so the choice is task-blind; without it, a reported score belongs to a mixture and cannot be reproduced by synthesising one compound.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A basic aliphatic amine appears in 82.2% of one panel's proposals, 100% of its top decile and 19.5% of its bottom decile, and in 94.3% of another panel's top decile, so the generator clearly can find basic nitrogen when it pays. But a piperidine or piperazine-type saturated N-heterocycle appears in only 0.5%, 0.1%, 0.6%, 3.9% and 0.1% of the five panels. The 1.0000-scoring leaders carry their basic nitrogen as an N-(4-aminobutyl) arm with a median of 7 rotatable bonds, and the 0.2299 macrocyclic leaders carry theirs as N-methyl amines inside a ten-membered ring rather than in a discrete six-membered one. Parent counts are the same within one proposal on every panel.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no route that cyclises a chain into a saturated nitrogen heterocycle, so basic amine centres are only ever presented on flexible open chains.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add a closure that cyclises an amine-bearing chain into a five-, six- or seven-membered saturated nitrogen ring, and its inverse. The existing close_ring operator is the lowest-weight of the seven and closes by graph distance without regard to what the resulting ring contains, which is why conformationally restricted basic centres stay out of reach while open-chain ones are abundant.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
